analysis:
Examined SandboxSetupProgress.swift (base and head) and the SandboxEligibilityTests.swift patch and base. The source change adds a `background` Bool to SandboxInstallerEvent, parsed from installer JSON at head line 107. It also adds a SandboxSizingPlan parser (head lines 131-185) that strictly decodes a single schema-1 `plan` line, and `waitingInBackground` renderer state (head lines 226, 245, 324, 349, 397-403). The only effect of that state is on the wording of the waitlist message.

The parsing is strictly typed (Int, Int64, Bool, String); a mismatch returns nil and the output is treated as text. Unknown fields are ignored. No new code execution, file or network access, credentials or privilege changes are introduced, and the plan parser does not execute anything.

Relevant threat TB-013 / T-061 (a tampered installer or add-on command runs as the Mac's owner): installer output was already untrusted in base. This PR adds only display-level fields. A malicious installer could already print arbitrary text, and it could already claim `background`; the only impact is a misleading "you can close this window" message. That is not a security regression, since the installer already runs as the owner and integrity is handled by the verification of the downloaded installer.

The terminal-injection surface is pre-existing: installer messages are printed raw. Head line 398 prints fixed text plus the CLI name. The new plan parser output is not rendered in the visible code. It is consumed by SandboxEligibility.estimatedPlan, which is not supplied and which this pass could not examine.

The test changes are refactors of the eligibility API (estimatedPlan, canRunJobs, refusal) with expectation updates. They do not affect security behavior. TB-012 / T-059 and the provider and inference threats are not touched by these files.

Remaining integration questions: where SandboxSizingPlan(line:) is invoked (installer `--plan` flags and how the process is run), how the plan numbers drive slot or disk decisions, and whether any plan value is passed to later install arguments. None of these callers is in the supplied evidence.
